newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Sony test markets tiny new GSM phone.
newsitem.headline: Sony test markets tiny new GSM phone.

text.p: Sony Corp on Thursday launched the worldwide test marketing of its CMD-Z1 GSM digital mobile telephone in an exclusive agreement with Czech GSM operator EuroTel spol s.r.o., officials of both companies said.

EuroTel will sell the handset, which Sony said was one of the smallest mobile phones ever produced, exclusively in the Czech Republic through the end of March after which it will be introduced elsewhere in Europe.
The CMD-Z1 GSM phone, the first solely Sony-designed and developed mobile phone, will have an introductory Czech price of 18,021 crowns.
Petra Klosova of Sony Czech Republic told a news conference the company selected the market because "of Sony's relatively great success" since the Czech network was lanched last July.
"Sony considers the Czech network as already very well developed," Klosova said.
The two Czech GSM networks launched last summer ended 1996 with roughly 150,000 users, according to company statistics.
The CMD-Z1 -- at 100 by 61.5 by 23.5 millimetres -- has a flip-down bar microphone which folds into the right side of the handset, and requires use of the left hand for normal phoning.
Its rechargable Lithium-Ion battery has a standby life of 80 hours or up to 10 hours of talk time in a single charge.
The unit also features what Sony calls the "jog dial", which, instead of a button, interfaces with a menu for faster scrolling through pre-set functions and recorded phone numbers.
EuroTel is a joint venture of Czech fixed-line monopoly operator SPT Telecom a.s., along with a U.S. consortium comprising Bell Atlantic Corp International, and U.S. West Media Group.
